description: Motor City Chemistry question bank for adaptive test generation

questions.question: What type of bond forms between Na and Cl?
questions.hint: Na is a metal, Cl is a nonmetal. Metals transfer electrons to nonmetals.

questions.question: What type of bond forms between two oxygen atoms?
questions.hint: Both atoms are nonmetals. Nonmetals share electrons.

questions.question: What type of bond forms between Ca and O?
questions.hint: Ca is a metal (Group 2), O is a nonmetal (Group 16).

questions.question: In an ionic bond, are electrons transferred or shared?
questions.hint: Ionic bonds form when one atom gives electrons to another.

questions.question: In a covalent bond, are electrons transferred or shared?
questions.hint: Covalent bonds form between nonmetals that share electron pairs.

questions.question: What type of bond forms between N and H?
questions.hint: Both are nonmetals, but they have different electronegativities.

questions.question: Is Al2O3 electrically neutral? Verify: Al is +3, O is -2.
Is Na2O3 electrically neutral? Na is +1, O is -2.
How many total atoms are in Al2(SO4)3?
questions.hint: 2 Al + 3 S + 12 O = 17. The subscript 3 multiplies everything in the parentheses.

questions.question: How many oxygen atoms are in Mg(NO3)2?
questions.hint: The subscript 2 multiplies everything inside: 3 O x 2 = 6 O.

questions.question: Write the formula for the ionic compound formed by Ca2+ and Cl-.
questions.hint: Ca is +2, Cl is -1. Need 2 Cl to balance: +2 + 2(-1) = 0.

questions.question: Write the formula for the ionic compound formed by Al3+ and O2-.
questions.hint: Cross the charges: Al needs subscript 2, O needs subscript 3. Check: 2(+3) + 3(-2) = 0.

questions.question: Write the formula for the ionic compound formed by Fe3+ and SO4 2-.
questions.hint: Cross charges: 2 Fe and 3 SO4. Parentheses around polyatomic ion when subscript > 1.

questions.question: Write the formula for the compound formed by NH4+ and Cl-.
questions.hint: Both charges are 1. 1:1 ratio. No parentheses needed.

questions.question: Write the formula for the compound formed by Ca2+ and PO4 3-.
questions.hint: Cross charges: 3 Ca and 2 PO4. Check: 3(+2) + 2(-3) = 0.

questions.question: In CuSO4, what is the charge on Cu?
questions.hint: SO4 is -2. For neutrality: Cu + (-2) = 0, so Cu = +2.

questions.question: In Fe2O3, what is the charge on Fe?
questions.hint: 3 O at -2 = -6 total. 2 Fe must equal +6. Each Fe = +3.

questions.question: Name: CaF2
questions.hint: Ca is always +2 (no Roman numeral). F root + -ide = fluoride.

questions.question: Name: Na2S
questions.hint: Na is Group 1 (always +1). S root + -ide = sulfide.

questions.question: Name: CuCl2
questions.hint: Cu is a transition metal. 2 Cl(-1) = -2, so Cu = +2. Must include (II).

questions.question: Name: Pb(NO3)2
questions.hint: Pb is a transition metal. 2 NO3(-1) = -2, so Pb = +2. NO3 = nitrate (polyatomic).

questions.question: Formula: Magnesium nitrate
questions.hint: Mg is +2, NO3 is -1. Need 2 nitrates. Parentheses required.

questions.question: Formula: Iron(III) oxide
questions.hint: Fe is +3 (Roman numeral III), O is -2. Cross: 2 Fe, 3 O.

questions.question: Formula: Ammonium sulfate
questions.hint: NH4 is +1, SO4 is -2. Need 2 ammonium ions. Parentheses around NH4.

questions.question: Name: CO2
questions.hint: Covalent naming uses prefixes. C has no prefix (mono- is dropped for first element). O gets di- (2).

questions.question: Name: N2O5
questions.hint: Both elements get prefixes: di- (2) for N, penta- (5) for O. O root + -ide.

questions.question: Name: PCl3
questions.hint: First element gets no prefix (just 1). Second element: tri- (3) + chlor + -ide.

questions.question: Formula: Sulfur hexafluoride
questions.hint: Sulfur = S (no prefix means 1). Hexa- = 6 fluorines.

questions.question: Formula: Dinitrogen monoxide
questions.hint: Di- = 2 nitrogen. Mono- = 1 oxygen.

questions.question: Name: SO3
questions.hint: First element no prefix. Second: tri- (3) + ox + -ide.

questions.question: How many valence electrons does oxygen have?
questions.hint: Oxygen is in Group 16. Group number minus 10 = valence electrons for p-block.

questions.question: How many valence electrons does nitrogen have?
questions.hint: Nitrogen is in Group 15. 15 - 10 = 5 valence electrons.

questions.question: How many total valence electrons are in H2O?
questions.hint: O has 6, each H has 1. Total: 6 + 1 + 1 = 8.

questions.question: How many total valence electrons are in CO2?
questions.hint: C has 4, each O has 6. Total: 4 + 6 + 6 = 16.

questions.question: How many lone pairs are on the central atom in H2O?
questions.hint: O has 6 valence e-. Uses 2 for bonds (2 H). Remaining 4 = 2 lone pairs.

questions.question: How many lone pairs are on the central atom in NH3?
questions.hint: N has 5 valence e-. Uses 3 for bonds (3 H). Remaining 2 = 1 lone pair.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of CH4?
questions.hint: 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs on C. Electron geometry = molecular geometry = tetrahedral.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of H2O?
questions.hint: 2 bonding pairs + 2 lone pairs on O. Lone pairs push bonds closer = bent shape.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of NH3?
questions.hint: 3 bonding pairs + 1 lone pair on N. Electron geometry is tetrahedral, molecular is pyramidal.

questions.question: What is the molecular geometry of CO2?
questions.hint: 2 bonding regions, 0 lone pairs on C. Bonds spread 180 degrees apart.

questions.question: What is the bond angle in a tetrahedral molecule?
questions.hint: 4 electron groups spread evenly in 3D space = 109.5 degree angles.

questions.question: Is H2O polar or nonpolar?
questions.hint: Bent shape means dipoles don't cancel. Asymmetric geometry = polar.
